title: Shared posting catalog vs tenant-private data
decision: Global postings catalog written by ONE platform crawler; per-tenant overlay rows for triage/score/report; project matches into each tenant's data/pipeline.md + data/scan-history.tsv so career-ops .mjs scripts keep files as SoT

schema.postings: posting_id PK, url_norm UNIQUE, ats_vendor, external_id, company, title, location, first_seen_global, last_seen, live_status
schema.tenant_posting_state: (tenant_id, posting_id) PK, first_seen_tenant, triage, score, report_num

why: The full-ATS sweep is the slowest operation and is byte-identical per tenant; per-tenant crawling is O(tenants x corpus) HTTP for zero added information.
side_benefit: Splitting first_seen_global from first_seen_tenant fixes the inbox freshness facet (career-ops.ts readScanDates), which today reads 'first seen by me' as if it were posting age.
constraints: Catalog is an INDEX, never a replacement for markdown SoT (volume-schema.json principle)
No cross-tenant inference from Class B data without explicit opt-in (AGENTS.md Source-of-Truth Boundary)
Postings remain untrusted input; sanitize once at ingest — sharing raises blast radius, not per-item risk
Move logo cache out of .career-ops-web/ (Class A living in a Class B directory)

alternatives_rejected.option: per-tenant crawl of the full ATS corpus
alternatives_rejected.why: duplicated cost/latency for identical public data
